options.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Asset: high fidelity WellBe object-material exploration sheet, landscape 3:2. Input image 1 is a style reference for the actual knowledge graph: use its delicate pastel, quiet small-object feeling and its soft cyan/teal tints. Input image 2 is a layout and interaction-reference sheet, NOT an edit target; its record circles are too flat and button-like. Generate a NEW concept sheet showing substantially more three-dimensional objects with a dynamic, responsive feel. This sheet should be useful to choose a real interactive UI direction.
Layout: near-white calm surface; a restrained teal WellBe wordmark top left, option title beside it. Left two-thirds: one elegant sparse map of six objects, completely readable dark navy labels, fine flowing association threads. Record labels exactly: "Monday note", "Visit summary", "Blood test", "Sleep note", "Lab attachment", "June capture". Use aqua for notes, pale lavender for documents, pale blue for results, grey for capture; color means record kind. Simple embossed or recessed glyphs consistent with reference: note, blank folded paper, filled bars, four small hub squares. The objects must look like small physical volumes, not flat disks, rings, UI buttons, plastic tokens, or coins. They should have real side curvature, delicate occlusion, and grounded soft shadows, readable front-facing glyphs, subtle physical depth; keep names on the flat page. Silky thin curved connections attach to the object sides and never enter unrelated circles or labels; two faint strands can bow under a drag, with one very restrained moving highlight suggested by a glint, no arrows. Do not use red, orange, amber, scores, diagnoses, galaxy/space imagery or a dark backdrop.
Right one-third, separated by a faint vertical rule: three clearly separated large closeups of the SAME aqua note object, labeled exactly "Rest", "Hover", "Drag". They must show genuine visibly different poses at the SAME apparent object size, not three identical static symbols: Rest sits slightly above the surface; Hover lifts and tilts toward a small pointer, moving its specular light and separating its contact shadow; Drag leans a little toward the pointer, with curved elastic attachments trailing smoothly and shadow offset. Demonstrate depth and local responsiveness through form, shade, glints and tether bending; NOT through motion-blur, duplicate ghost objects, decorative orbit rings, or broad glow. Keep each label legible and unobstructed. No large explanatory paragraphs, no extra dashboard controls. Sophisticated, warm, personal, tactile, plausible UI.
Option title verbatim: "A · Floating porcelain". Material direction: sculpted satin ceramic near-spheres, a much rounder crown than the old flattened domes, a visibly rounded side falling to a soft tucked-under rim. Pearl-white upper light, restrained pastel tint collecting in the underside, tiny soft specular crescent and subtle surface texture. Stronger physical depth than the reference but still quiet, like a little polished ceramic stone floating 4–8 pixels above a matte white desk. No thick outer ring, no flat coin faces. The glyph is lightly recessed into the curved surface with a fine inner shadow and white bevel. Tilt on Hover reveals a little more of one curved side, with a small moving highlight; Drag shows weight and elastic tension. This should be the closest elegant evolution of the existing knowledge graph.

Option title verbatim: "B · Frosted pearl". Material direction: a softly frosted translucent near-spherical pearl with a lightly opaque luminous pastel core. A very thin optical shell, realistic depth from refraction and curved sidewalls, restrained internal scattering, clear volume, gentle caustic directly below it. Mostly frosted/satin, not glossy glass marbles, not soap bubbles, not gemstone jewels, no metallic iridescence. Keep color coding stable; use the assigned aqua/lavender/blue, very light and quiet. The glyph appears inset slightly within the front skin but stays sharp and readable. Hover gives noticeable parallax between glyph, shell highlight and internal core. Drag shifts the inner light slightly behind the shell and gently stretches the smooth tether lines while preserving the circular volume. Elegant airy dimensionality distinctly different from ceramic.

Option title verbatim: "C · Living pebble". Material direction: a velvety glazed ceramic/silicone hybrid, a soft plump pebble with a quietly organic near-circular silhouette and convincing full 3D volume; NOT a puddle, jelly blob, amoeba, candy, or inflated toy. Its shape can change only 2–4 percent with a subtle breathing quality. The central glyph stays sharp, calm, pressed into the front curve, and readable. Rest is softly rounded and almost circular; Hover gently tips and seems to inhale toward the pointer, with a shifted contact patch and highlight; Drag has a very small directional squash and stretch, a tiny lean with weight and elastic recovery, with smoothly bending attachments that pull at the side. The surface is richer and more tactile than the other options, never wet/glossy. Warm gentle depth, sparse map, realistic soft shadows. The living quality should come from changing weight, curvature and local light, not from decorative animation symbols.
